title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 3 Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
short_title: Class 10 Maths · Ch 3 Pair of Linear Equations
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.L1: Nature of solutions from the ratios / lines
patterns.L2: Find k for a number of solutions

S1.name: Consistent, inconsistent, dependent pairs
S1.tip: Intersecting lines: one solution (consistent). Parallel: no solution (inconsistent). Coincident: infinitely many (dependent, still consistent).

S2.name: The ratio test
S2.tip: Write both equations as ax + by + c = 0 first. a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2 → unique; all three ratios equal → infinitely many; first two equal, third different → none.

S3.name: Find k (or a, b) for a number of solutions
S3.tip: Set the ratios the condition needs equal, solve for k, then always check the third ratio (c1/c2) for 'no solution' or 'infinitely many'.

S4.name: Graphical method
S4.tip: Plot two points per line (use x = 0 and y = 0), read the meeting point, and use y = 0 for points on the x-axis when a triangle is asked.

S5.name: Substitution method
S5.tip: Make one variable the subject of one equation, put it into the other, solve, then substitute back. Verify in both equations.

S6.name: Elimination method
S6.tip: Multiply to make one coefficient equal, then add or subtract. If both variables vanish: a false statement → no solution, a true one → infinitely many.

S7.name: Word problems: ages, fractions, digits
S7.tip: Name the unknowns, turn each sentence into one equation (ages: add or subtract the same years from both), solve and check the story.

S8.name: Word problems: money, marks, charges
S8.tip: Fixed charge + rate × quantity: write one equation per given case and subtract to remove the fixed charge.

S9.name: Case study and given-solution questions
S9.tip: Given a solution: substitute it into both equations. Case studies: define x and y in words, form both equations, then answer each part.
S9.ncert: Case-study type (SQP 2026-27 Q36); past-paper one-mark type

questions.question: A pair of linear equations whose lines are parallel has:
A pair of linear equations is called consistent when it has:
questions.explanation: Consistent = one solution or infinitely many.

questions.question: If the lines of a pair coincide, the pair is:
questions.explanation: Coincident lines: every point common, so dependent; a dependent pair is always consistent.

questions.question: The pair y = 0 and y = −7 has:
questions.explanation: Both lines are horizontal and parallel.

questions.question: The lines x = 3 and y = −2 meet at:
questions.explanation: x = 3 is vertical, y = −2 horizontal: they meet once, at (3, −2).

questions.question: For a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, a unique solution exists when:
questions.explanation: Different slopes → the lines intersect once.

The lines 3x + 6y − 9 = 0 and x + 2y − 3 = 0 are:

questions.question: Find k so that 3x − y + 8 = 0 and 6x − ky + 16 = 0 have infinitely many solutions.
Find k so that 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + ky = 10 have no solution.

For infinitely many solutions of 2x + 3y = 7 and (a − 1)x + (a + 1)y = 3a − 1, find a.
questions.explanation: 2/(a − 1) = 3/(a + 1) → 2a + 2 = 3a − 3 → a = 5. Check the third ratio: 7/(3a − 1) = 7/14 = 1/2, the same as 2/4 and 3/6.

questions.question: For what value of k do kx − y − 2 = 0 and 6x − 2y − 3 = 0 have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: k = 3 matches a1/a2 = b1/b2 = 1/2, but c1/c2 = 2/3. All three can never be equal.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: always check the third ratio (2026 board item).

questions.question: In the graphical method, the solution of the pair is:
questions.explanation: A solution lies on both lines.
options: the point where the two lines meet
the y-intercept of the first line

questions.question: The lines x + 3y = 6 and 2x − 3y = 12 meet at:
The lines x − y + 1 = 0 and 3x + 2y − 12 = 0 form a triangle with the x-axis. Find the x-coordinate of the vertex that is not on the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Solving: x = y − 1 → 3y − 3 + 2y = 12 → y = 3, x = 2. Vertex (2, 3).

questions.question: Find the area (in square units) of the triangle formed by x − y = −2, 3x + y = 6 and the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Meet at (1, 3); x-axis points (−2, 0) and (2, 0); area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6.

questions.question: The lines 2x + y = 6 and 2x − y = 2 cut the x-axis at:
Solve x + y = 14 and x − y = 4 by substitution. What is x?
Solve 2x + 3y = 11 and 2x − 4y = −24. Then find m if y = mx + 3.
Using substitution on x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 12, you get −4 = 0. This means the pair has:
questions.explanation: A false statement with no variable → parallel lines → no solution. (NCERT Example 7, the rails.)

questions.question: Solve by elimination: 3x + 2y = 16 and 3x − 2y = 8. What is y?
If 2x + y = 13 and 4x − y = 17, find x − y.
questions.explanation: Add: 6x = 30 → x = 5, y = 3, so x − y = 2. (2024 board item.)

questions.question: If 217x + 131y = 913 and 131x + 217y = 827, find x.
questions.explanation: Add: x + y = 5. Subtract: x − y = 1. So x = 3, y = 2. (2023 board item.)
